extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED/USPTO officials, hearing officers, and attorneys representing parties
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements governing disciplinary investigations, complaints, motions, service, disposition, transfer to disability inactive status, diversion, reactivation/reinstatement, and conduct of hearings for practitioners before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to hold proceeding in abeyance for incapacity
rubrics_metrics.description: In the course of a disciplinary proceeding under § 11.32, the practitioner may file a motion requesting the hearing officer to enter an order holding such proceeding in abeyance based on the contention that the practitioner is suffering from a disability or addiction that makes it impossible for the practitioner to adequately defend the charges in the disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motion is available while a disciplinary proceeding is pending and is premised on disability/addiction rendering defense impossible. See § 11.28(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of practitioner's motion for abeyance
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner's motion shall, in addition to any other requirement of § 11.43, include or have attached thereto: (A) A brief statement of all material facts; (B) Affidavits, medical reports, official records, or other documents and the opinion of at least one medical expert setting forth and establishing any of the material facts on which the practitioner is relying; (C) A statement that the practitioner acknowledges the alleged incapacity by reason of disability or addiction; (D) Written consent by the practitioner to be transferred to disability inactive status if the motion is granted; and (E) Written agreement by the practitioner not to practice before the Office in patent, trademark, or other non-patent matters while in disability inactive status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed items are mandatory attachments/inclusions to the motion; medical expert opinion required; explicit consent and agreement not to practice while inactive are prerequisites for abeyance motions. See § 11.28(a)(1)(i)(A)-(E).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director response to practitioner's motion
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director's response shall be served and filed within thirty days after service of the practitioner's motion (unless time modified) and shall set forth: (A) All objections, if any; (B) An admission, denial or allegation of lack of knowledge with respect to each of the material facts; and (C) Affidavits, medical reports, official records, or other documents setting forth facts on which the OED Director intends to rely for disputing or denying any material fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response deadline is 30 days unless shortened/enlarged; must address each material fact and attach documentary evidence if disputing. See § 11.28(a)(1)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting motion to hold in abeyance
rubrics_metrics.description: The motion shall be granted upon a showing of good cause to believe the practitioner to be incapacitated as alleged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing officer decides on motion and response; 'good cause' standard applies. In addiction cases, order may include conditions before return to active status. See § 11.28(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects when abeyance granted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the required showing is made, the hearing officer shall enter an order holding the disciplinary proceeding in abeyance; upon receipt of the order, the OED Director shall transfer the practitioner to disability inactive status, give notice to the practitioner, cause notice to be published, and give notice to appropriate authorities in the Office that the practitioner has been placed in disability inactive status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner must comply with § 11.58 and shall not engage in practice before the Office until a determination is made to resume practice. Permission for paralegal activity requires OED Director approval and compliance with § 11.58(h). See § 11.28(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for reactivation frequency and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any practitioner transferred to disability inactive status in a disciplinary proceeding may file with the hearing officer a motion for reactivation once a year beginning at any time not less than one year after the initial effective date of inactivation, or once during any shorter interval provided by the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reactivation frequency may be reduced by the order; if granted, the disciplinary proceeding resumes under schedule established by hearing officer. See § 11.28(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required for motion for reactivation
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion by the practitioner for reactivation alleging recovery from prior disability or addiction shall be accompanied by all available medical reports or similar documents related thereto. The hearing officer may require other necessary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical documentation is required; hearing officer has discretion to request additional proof. See § 11.28(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's motion to resume proceedings from abeyance
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, having good cause to believe a practitioner is no longer incapacitated, may file a motion requesting the hearing officer to terminate a prior order holding a pending proceeding in abeyance because of the practitioner's disability or addiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED Director bears burden of showing by clear and convincing evidence that practitioner is able to defend; if genuine issue of material fact, hearing officer will hold evidentiary hearing. See § 11.28(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner's response to OED Director motion to resume
rubrics_metrics.description: If the hearing officer requires the practitioner to file a response, the practitioner must present clear and convincing evidence that the prior self-alleged disability or addiction continues to make it impossible for the practitioner to defend in the underlying proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden shifts to practitioner to show continued incapacity by clear and convincing evidence when directed. See § 11.28(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing officer authority to reactivate practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: If the hearing officer determines there is good cause to believe the practitioner is not incapacitated from defending or practicing before the Office, the hearing officer shall take such action as deemed appropriate, including entry of an order directing reactivation and resumption of the disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing officer may order reactivation and resume proceedings if incapacity no longer shown. See § 11.28(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify OED Director of out-of-jurisdiction disability transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of being transferred to disability inactive status in another jurisdiction, a practitioner subject to the disciplinary jurisdiction of the Office shall notify the OED Director in writing of the transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED Director will obtain certified copy of order and may file a request with USPTO Director for reciprocal transfer. See § 11.29(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement for judicial declarations/orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of being judicially declared incompetent, involuntarily committed after a hearing on grounds of incompetency or disability, or placed by court order under guardianship or conservatorship in another jurisdiction, a practitioner shall notify the OED Director in writing of such judicial action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED Director will obtain certified copy and may request transfer to disability inactive status with USPTO Director. See § 11.29(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO notice to practitioner on receipt of out-of-jurisdiction order
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a certified copy of an order or declaration from another jurisdiction demonstrating transfer to disability inactive status or similar judicial actions, together with the OED Director's request, the USPTO Director shall issue a notice directed to the practitioner containing a copy of the order and an order directing the practitioner to file a response within 40 days establishing by clear and convincing evidence a genuine issue of material fact that transfer would be unwarranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response must be supported by affidavit and address grounds listed in § 11.29(d)(1)(i)-(iv). See § 11.29(b) and (b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to oppose reciprocal/initial transfer to disability inactive status
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may avoid transfer by demonstrating by clear and convincing evidence, or showing genuine issue of material fact by clear and convincing evidence, that: (i) the procedure was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute a deprivation of due process; (ii) there was such infirmity of proof establishing the transfer or judicial action that the USPTO Director could not accept the conclusion; (iii) imposition of the same disability status would result in grave injustice; or (iv) the practitioner is not the individual transferred or declared incompetent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the specific defenses the USPTO Director will consider on the documentary record or, if a genuine issue exists, may deny the request and proceed to further action. See § 11.29(d)(1)(i)-(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof for USPTO Director decisions on transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall impose transfer unless the practitioner demonstrates by clear and convincing evidence, or the USPTO Director finds a genuine issue of material fact by clear and convincing evidence, as to the enumerated defenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear and convincing evidence standard applies to practitioner’s showing to avoid transfer; if no genuine issue, USPTO Director shall enter final order. See § 11.29(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of adjudication in other jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: A final adjudication in another jurisdiction that a practitioner be transferred to disability inactive status, is judicially declared incompetent, is judicially ordered to be involuntarily committed on grounds of incompetency or disability, or is placed by court order under guardianship or conservatorship shall establish the disability for purposes of a reciprocal transfer to or transfer to disability status before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final orders elsewhere are given conclusive effect for reciprocal transfer purposes absent the enumerated defenses. See § 11.29(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate and indefinite effect of transfer order
rubrics_metrics.description: An order by the USPTO Director imposing reciprocal transfer to disability inactive status or transferring a practitioner to disability inactive status shall be effective immediately and shall be for an indefinite period until further order of the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy of order must be served on practitioner, guardian, and/or institution director; practitioner shall comply with the section and § 11.58 and not practice unless reinstated. See § 11.29(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of disability proceedings and publicity of orders
rubrics_metrics.description: All proceedings involving allegations of disability shall be kept confidential until and unless the USPTO Director enters an order transferring the practitioner to disability inactive status. The OED Director shall publicize any transfer in the same manner as for the imposition of public discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings are confidential until transfer order; thereafter orders are publicized. See § 11.29(h)(1)-(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission for paralegal employment while on disability inactive status
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner in disability inactive status must obtain permission from the OED Director to engage in paralegal activity permitted under § 11.58(h); permission will be granted only if the practitioner has complied with all the conditions of § 11.58 applicable to disability inactive status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If permission granted, practitioner must fully comply with § 11.58(h). See § 11.29(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition frequency and process
rubrics_metrics.description: No practitioner transferred to disability inactive status may resume active status except by order of the OED Director. A practitioner shall be entitled to petition the OED Director for transfer to active status once a year, or at whatever shorter intervals the USPTO Director may direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon petition, OED Director may direct examination by qualified medical/psychological experts at practitioner's expense and require disclosure and written consent to release records. See § 11.29(j)(1)-(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosures for reinstatement petition
rubrics_metrics.description: With the filing of a petition for reinstatement to active status, the practitioner shall be required to disclose the name of each psychiatrist, psychologist, physician and hospital or other institution by whom or in which the practitioner has been examined or treated for the disability since the transfer; and furnish written consent to the release of information and records relating to the incapacity if requested by the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure and waiver of privilege are mandatory for consideration; failure to provide may impede reinstatement. See § 11.29(j)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of competence and learning in law for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may direct that the practitioner establish proof of competence and learning in law, which proof may include passing the registration examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED Director has discretion to require substantive proof of legal competence in addition to medical evidence. See § 11.29(j)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting reinstatement to active status
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall grant the petition for transfer to active status upon a showing by clear and convincing evidence that the incapacity has been removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear and convincing evidence required to show incapacity removed before returning to active status. See § 11.29(j)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversion program eligibility (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before or after a complaint is filed, the OED Director may dispose of a disciplinary matter by entering into a diversion agreement; neither the OED Director nor the practitioner is under any obligation to propose or enter into a diversion agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversion agreements may provide law office management assistance, counseling, participation in lawyer assistance programs, and CLE. Eligibility rules apply. See § 11.30(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversion program disqualification by prior discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for diversion, a practitioner cannot have been disciplined by the USPTO or another jurisdiction within the past three years, except that discipline by another jurisdiction is not disqualifying if that discipline was based on the conduct forming the basis for the current investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recent discipline (within 3 years) bars eligibility unless it's the same conduct under investigation. See § 11.30(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversion program disqualifying conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: For a practitioner to be eligible for diversion, the conduct at issue must not involve: (1) misappropriation of funds or dishonesty, deceit, fraud, or misrepresentation; (2) substantial prejudice to a client or other person; (3) a serious crime as defined in § 11.1; or (4) a pattern of similar misconduct unless the misconduct at issue is minor and related to a chronic physical or mental health condition or disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed categories of misconduct preclude diversion eligibility; limited exception for minor pattern related to chronic health condition. See § 11.30(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of successful completion of diversion agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The diversion agreement is automatically completed when the terms of the agreement have been fulfilled. A practitioner's successful completion bars the OED Director from pursuing discipline based on the conduct set forth in the diversion agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion constitutes final disposition as to the conduct covered by the agreement. See § 11.30(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of material breach of diversion agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A material breach of the diversion agreement shall be cause for termination of the practitioner's participation in the diversion program. Upon a material breach, the OED Director may pursue discipline based on the conduct set forth in the diversion agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material breach reopens the possibility of formal disciplinary action on the covered conduct. See § 11.30(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of disciplinary proceeding after investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: If after conducting an investigation under § 11.22(a), the OED Director is of the opinion that grounds exist for discipline under § 11.19(b), the OED Director may convene a meeting of a panel of the Committee on Discipline to determine whether there is probable cause to bring disciplinary charges; if the panel finds probable cause, the OED Director may institute a disciplinary proceeding by filing a complaint under § 11.34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel of the Committee on Discipline evaluates probable cause before formal complaint can be filed. See § 11.32.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of complaint instituting disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint shall: (1) Name the person who is the subject; (2) Give a plain and concise description of the respondent's alleged grounds for discipline; (3) State the place and time, not less than thirty days from the date the complaint is filed, for filing an answer; (4) State that a decision by default may be entered if an answer is not timely filed; and (5) Be signed by the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint must fairly inform respondent and, where applicable, identify USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct forming the basis so respondent can prepare a defense. See § 11.34(a)-(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing a complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint shall be filed within one year after the date on which the OED Director receives a grievance forming the basis of the complaint. No complaint shall be filed more than ten years after the date on which the misconduct forming the basis for the proceeding occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-year filing period may be tolled by written agreement between practitioner and OED Director. See § 11.34(d)-(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of service of complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint may be served by: (1) personal delivery with affidavit of service; (2) mailing by Priority Mail Express®, first-class mail, or a delivery service providing confirmation of delivery or attempted delivery to addresses as specified; (3) any mutually agreeable method; or (4) for respondents outside the U.S., by a delivery service providing confirmation of delivery or attempted delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If copy cannot be delivered through these methods, OED Director shall publish notice in Official Gazette for two consecutive weeks, and time for filing answer is 30 days from second publication. Service on attorney of record is permitted. See § 11.35(a)-(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to answer complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file an answer will constitute an admission of the allegations in the complaint and may result in entry of default judgment; every allegation not denied is deemed admitted and may be considered proven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing officer may enter initial decision on default if no answer; respondents must timely respond to avoid admission by default. See § 11.36(d)-(e) and § 11.35(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of answer to complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The answer shall include a statement of the facts that constitute the grounds of defense and shall specifically admit or deny each allegation set forth in the complaint; must not deny a material allegation known to be true or claim lack of information when respondent possesses it; must state affirmatively special matters of defense and any intent to raise a disability as a mitigating factor, specifying the defense or disability, its nexus to the misconduct, and the reason it provides a defense or mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to specify special matters or disability in the answer precludes reliance on them later, absent hearing officer's good-cause allowance for late filing. See § 11.36(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contested case status and subpoena evidence rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the filing of an answer by the respondent, a disciplinary proceeding shall be regarded as a contested case within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 24. Evidence obtained by a subpoena issued under 35 U.S.C. 24 shall not be admitted into the record or considered unless leave to proceed under 35 U.S.C. 24 was previously authorized by the hearing officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoenaed evidence has special admissibility constraints tied to hearing officer authorization. See § 11.38.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing officer designation, independence, and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing officer designated by the USPTO Director shall conduct disciplinary proceedings; the hearing officer shall not be subject to first- or second-level supervision by the USPTO Director or OED Director, shall not be supervised by investigators/prosecutors, shall be impartial and not have participated in decision to initiate proceedings, and shall be either an administrative law judge appointed under 5 U.S.C. 3105 or an attorney designated under 35 U.S.C. 32 possessing suitable experience and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing officer independence and impartiality are mandated to ensure fair adjudication. See § 11.39(a)-(b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing officer responsibilities and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer shall have authority to administer oaths, rule on motions, receive relevant evidence and examine witnesses, authorize depositions, determine time/place of hearings and regulate conduct, hold conferences, receive oral/written arguments, adopt/modify procedures for orderly disposition, make initial decisions under §§ 11.25 and 11.54, and take measures to promote efficient, timely, and impartial conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive list of procedural powers to manage disciplinary proceedings. See § 11.39(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time expectation for initial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer shall set times and exercise control over proceedings such that an initial decision under § 11.54 is normally issued within nine months of the date a complaint is filed, although the hearing officer may issue an initial decision later if circumstances preclude issuance within nine months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nine-month target is normative but not absolute. See § 11.39(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of interlocutory orders by USPTO Director
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director will not review an interlocutory order of a hearing officer except (1) when the hearing officer believes the order involves a controlling question of procedure or law with substantial ground for difference of opinion and immediate decision may materially advance termination, or (2) in an extraordinary situation where the USPTO Director deems justice requires review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited interlocutory review preserves hearing officer authority but allows review in narrow circumstances. See § 11.39(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: No ex parte merits discussions with hearing officer
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer shall engage in no ex parte discussions with any party on the merits of the complaint, beginning with appointment and ending when the final agency decision is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits communications that could compromise impartiality. See § 11.39(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation by attorney and attorney declaration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may represent himself or herself, or be represented by an attorney before the Office; the attorney shall file a written declaration that he or she is an attorney within the meaning of § 11.1 and shall state the address for correspondence and a telephone number reachable during normal business hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorney of record must file contact information and declaration per § 11.40(a). Service on attorney of record permitted. See § 11.40 and § 11.35(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and screening rules for OED/USPTO counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: The Deputy General Counsel for Intellectual Property and Solicitor and attorneys in the Office of the Solicitor shall represent the OED Director and shall not consult with the USPTO Director, General Counsel, Deputy General Counsel for General Law, or an individual designated by the USPTO Director to decide disciplinary matters regarding the proceeding. The General Counsel and Deputy General Counsel for General Law shall remain screened from investigation and prosecution to be available as counsel to the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical screening and separation of functions to preserve impartial decision-making and counsel availability. See § 11.40(b)-(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing location and timing of papers in disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers filed after the complaint and prior to entry of an initial decision shall be filed with the hearing officer at an address or place designated by the hearing officer. All papers filed after entry of an initial decision shall be filed with the USPTO Director. 'Filed' means delivery, mailing, or electronic transmission to a hearing officer or designee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal filing rules in other parts of chapter (§§ 1.8 and 2.197) do not apply; hearing officer may prescribe means of filing. See § 11.41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service methods for papers other than complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers other than a complaint shall be served on a respondent represented by an attorney by (1) delivering a copy to the attorney's office, (2) mailing by first-class mail, Priority Mail Express®, or other delivery service to the attorney's address provided under § 11.40(a)(1), or (3) any other mutually agreeable method; for unrepresented respondents, similar methods apply directed to respondent. Each paper filed shall contain a certificate of service indicating date and method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing officer or USPTO Director may require hand service or Priority Mail Express; service by mail is completed when placed in custody of USPS. See § 11.42(a)-(f).
